title: The Last Spire Anew
premise: Gideon Halloran, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead, has spent his life in the Hollow Vale, a valley where magic cannot follow and where his gift falls silent. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley to seize anyone touched by the old covenant, Gideon flees into a world where dragon-fire is guttering out and the dead grow louder by the day. Guided by a disgraced huntress, a runaway priest, and the ghost of a murdered dragon-warden, he learns that the covenant binding realms was broken deliberately—by the crown itself—to hoard magic. To end the hunt and quiet the restless dead, Gideon must carry a shard of living bone to the Last Spire and reforge the covenant, sacrificing his own ability to hear the dead forever. In the final act he succeeds at terrible cost: the realms are rejoined, his found family survives him, but Gideon becomes the first of the silent dead—a guardian voice that can no longer be heard, only felt.
about_author: Odile Okonkwo is a former archivist who grew up between two countries and two languages, and writes about people who belong fully to neither. She lives near a river she refuses to name, carving small figures from driftwood.

chapters.title: The Quiet Valley
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the Hollow Vale, Gideon carves memorial bones for the grieving, though here his gift is mute and he only pretends to hear. We meet his adoptive mother Maren and the rhythms of valley life. Emotional beat: contentment built on self-erasure—he has made silence his home.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Bone
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A traveler's keepsake crosses the valley border, and for the first time in years Gideon hears a dead woman's voice begging him to warn 'the warden.' Frightened, he nearly burns the bone. Emotional beat: longing—the gift he buried still lives, and it terrifies and thrills him.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Crown riders post a decree: all gifted persons must be surrendered or hunted. The valley elders vote to comply, choosing safety over their neighbors. Maren quietly packs Gideon's satchel. Emotional beat: betrayal—the community that sheltered him sells its principles for peace.

chapters.title: What Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Hunt-captain Serah Vane arrives early; Maren dies buying Gideon time to flee through the mist-line where magic fails. Crossing over, the dead's voices crash over him like a flood. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose—he carries her last words like a coal.

chapters.title: The Huntress Who Quit
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Vane, disillusioned after burning a village of innocents, tracks Gideon not to capture but to question—and finds his gift undeniable. She lets him go, deserting the hunt. Emotional beat: moral rupture—an instrument of the law chooses conscience over orders.

chapters.title: Road of Small Ghosts
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Traveling with Serah against his better judgment, Gideon passes villages where children born without gifts are branded 'hollow' and exiled. He takes in a hollow boy, Tam. Emotional beat: compassion hardening into resolve—the hunt's cruelty is systemic, not incidental.

chapters.title: The Priest Who Unbelieved
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. A former royal chaplain, Anselm fled after discovering church archives proving the covenant was broken on purpose. He seeks Gideon, whose carved bone shard matches an artifact in the records. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption through dangerous truth-telling.

chapters.title: Archive of Ashes
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. In a burned monastery, Anselm shows them evidence: the crown severed the covenant a century ago to monopolize magic, and the dying dragons are the seal failing. The dead grow louder because the boundary frays. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything—the hunt is a cover-up.

chapters.title: The Warden's Grave
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Following the ghost's plea, they find the murdered dragon-warden's tomb; her spirit names Gideon's bone shard as a covenant-key and warns that the Last Spire must be reached before the final dragon-fire gutters—at midwinter. Emotional beat: inheritance—a stranger's death becomes his charge.

chapters.title: Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The found family coalesces around campfires: Serah teaching Tam to fight, Anselm teaching him letters, Gideon teaching him to listen without fear. But bounty notices spread with Gideon's face. Emotional beat: warmth under threat—belonging discovered precisely when it becomes most dangerous.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Her former lieutenant corners them at a bridge; Serah offers herself as bait so the others escape, and is captured. Gideon refuses to abandon her. Emotional beat: loyalty tested—rescuing her means walking into the trap she built to save them.

chapters.title: Ironhold
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Infiltrating the fortress city, Gideon hears thousands of dead pressed into the crown's soul-vaults, harvested to fuel the hunt's anti-magic engines. He frees a fragment, alerting the realm's spirits to his existence. Emotional beat: horror and awe—the scale of the crown's theft revealed.

chapters.title: What the Dead Ask
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The freed dead offer power enough to destroy Ironhold—if Gideon will let them ride him. Tempted by vengeance for Maren, he refuses; they part in anger, and the voices go cold. Emotional beat: temptation refused at cost—justice outside the law cannot mean becoming the law's mirror.

chapters.title: The Breaking of Serah Vane
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Interrogated by her old commander, Serah learns the hunt's true order: not containment but extermination before the covenant can be reforged. She escapes with Anselm's help, wounded and stripped of every illusion about the crown. Emotional beat: disillusion completed—loyalty to truth finally outweighs loyalty to uniform.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Snow
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The scattered company reunites in a mountain pass; Tam, left behind as lookout, must choose between hiding safely and signaling them past an ambush. He signals, saving them, and earns his place. Emotional beat: courage of the smallest member—the found family holds because each chooses it.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They reach the dragon Eyrrith, dying atop the Last Spire, fire down to embers. She shows Gideon the reforge requires a living key: someone who hears the dead must become the hinge between realms, permanently silent. Emotional beat: dread of the price—the quest's goal is also his ending.

chapters.title: Arguments at the End of the World
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. The companions fight over whether to let Gideon sacrifice himself; Anselm searches the archives for an alternative and finds none, only precedent. Gideon, listening to Maren's remembered words, accepts. Emotional beat: love arguing with fate—and losing honestly.

chapters.title: The Crown Arrives
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. The hunt's full force scales the Spire to kill the last dragon and bury the truth forever. Serah, in her old uniform one last time, walks out alone to stall the army while Gideon works. Emotional beat: defiance—she stands between the law and justice, and picks a side.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Climax. Amid battle, Gideon sets the shard into the Spire's heart and speaks the covenant with every dead voice he has ever heard joining him—including, briefly, Maren's. The realms knit together; dragon-fire roars back; the anti-magic engines die. Gideon begins to fade. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender—his gift becomes the world's healing.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The hunt collapses as the truth spreads; survivors of the Spire descend into a changed world where magic returns and the branded 'hollow' are unbranded. Tam carries Gideon's unfinished carvings. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope—the world saved, the saver gone.

chapters.title: The Silent Guardian
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Months later, Serah and Anselm testify before a provisional council; the valley opens its borders at last. At the mist-line, Serah feels a presence she cannot hear—warm, watchful, unmistakably Gideon. Emotional beat: bittersweet communion—love persisting beyond speech.

chapters.title: Carved in Living Bone
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, epilogue. Now a carver himself, Tam finishes Gideon's last piece and leaves it at the Spire. Across the realm, the dead rest quietly, and travelers report a feeling of being watched over in the high passes. Emotional beat: legacy—the found family carries the work forward, and the silent dead are never truly gone.
